A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical research and contain readable main text, five figures, and Appendix A.1–A.6. The complete material supports comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports definitions, theorems, proofs, and constructed graph examples, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis results.

after.justification: V2 remains theoretical. Its revised assumptions and proofs and retained graph illustrations do not constitute empirical results.

M1.justification: The three do-calculus rules and the SC-projection and SC-hedge constructions remain unchanged. The revisions concern their assumptions and theoretical justification, rather than a changed identification procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets, populations, or empirical tasks. The constructed graph examples are retained; the expanded theoretical scope is assessed under T1.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. Discussions of ordinary hedges, cluster-ADMGs, and summary causal graphs remain theoretical comparisons.

E3.justification: Neither version contains empirical evaluation protocols, data splits, training budgets, or experimental metrics.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, or empirical supplementary analyses are added or removed. The illustrative examples and the cluster-size counterexample in Section 4 and Figure 5 are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: There are no empirical result entries to update. Examples 1–5 and Figures 2–5 retain their identification conclusions and illustrative causal-effect formulas; changes to theoretical guarantees are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Assumption 1 replaces the requirement that every known cluster contain more than one variable with the weaker condition that no adjacent clusters in a cycle are both singletons. Appendix A.3 correspondingly identifies the two constructed vertices for singleton clusters, expanding the stated scope of Theorems 2, 4, and 5. Section 2 also removes the assumptions that exogenous variables are independent and enter at most two structural equations. Definition 5 corrects the comparison of interventional distributions from Pr1 versus itself to Pr1 versus Pr2.

C1.justification: The headline contributions remain soundness and completeness of d-separation and do-calculus and SC-hedge characterization of non-identifiability. V2 makes the previously assumed ADMG setting and cluster-size qualification explicit in the abstract. The broader formal assumption is not consistently propagated to the abstract, introduction, or conclusion.

C2.justification: V2 discusses applicability under the weaker cluster-size condition, notes that positivity can be relaxed, and explicitly distinguishes assumption-independent soundness in Theorems 1 and 3 from assumption-dependent results in Theorems 2, 4, and 5. The warning that SC-hedge completeness remains unproved already appeared in v1's conclusion.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies code or data access instructions, implementation settings, hardware specifications, or computational resource information. No such disclosures are added or removed.

R1.justification: V2 adds Assaad et al. (2023), Tikka et al. (2023), and Hwang et al. (2024) in discussions of partial causal graphs, clustering, and positivity. The overall research positioning remains unchanged. The updated Assaad (2025) reference corresponds to the previously cited work.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper to emphasize 'a C-DMG over ADMGs', updates terminology and notation, corrects grammatical errors, and adds brief explanations. The section organization and Appendix A.1–A.6 structure remain intact.

P2.justification: All five figures retain their graphical content. Figure 4 moves from before Theorem 4 in v1 to within Section 3.3 in v2, accompanied by text reflow and small caption and typesetting edits. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: V2 improves precision through the Definition 5 correction, clearer ADMG terminology, and explicit theorem dependencies. However, Assumption 1 and Appendix A.3 adopt a weaker singleton condition while the abstract and introduction retain the earlier restriction and the conclusion still describes the adopted condition as a possible future relaxation. Section 2 also removes exogenous-variable assumptions without explaining the consequences. These unresolved changes to mathematical premises and scope prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
